updates.bio: Research soil scientist with the USDA-ARS Range Management Research Unit in Las Cruces since 1998 and a long-time co-PI of the Jornada Basin LTER. updates.name: Jeffrey M. Warren
updates.bio: Senior staff scientist at Oak Ridge National Laboratory since 2010, who also holds adjunct faculty status at the University of Tennessee-Knoxville. A tree physiologist by training, he studies how drought, fire and insect disturbance alter plant physiology, water movement between soil and plants, and ecosystem function; he also images roots and soils with neutrons and X-rays.
updates.research_interests: ecosystem responses to abiotic and biotic disturbance (drought, fire, insects); plant physiology; soil-plant water relations; ecosystem function; urban energy balance; neutron, gamma and X-ray imaging of pyrolysis, soil hydrodynamics and rhizosphere exchanges

updates.name: Jeffrey Q. Chambers
updates.bio: Professor of Geography at UC Berkeley and faculty scientist in Berkeley Lab's Climate and Ecosystem Sciences Division. He works on terrestrial ecosystem ecology, forest responses to climate change, disturbance and recovery, and land-atmosphere exchange, using field physiology, remote sensing and simulation models at sites spanning Puerto Rico, Panama, California and the Brazilian Amazon.
updates.research_interests: biogeography and the biosphere; forests and climate change; vegetation dynamics and remote sensing; disturbance and recovery processes; land-atmosphere interactions

updates.bio: Harold Bailey Professor of Biological Sciences at Virginia Tech since 1994 and the department's graduate director since 2011, following faculty posts in zoology at NC State. A behavioral ecologist and conservation biologist, he studies cooperative breeding in birds, dispersal, sensitivity to habitat fragmentation, and conservation of endangered birds. Elected Fellow of the American Ornithologists' Union.
updates.research_interests: evolution of cooperative breeding in birds; ecological basis of sensitivity to habitat fragmentation; social behavior and life history in birds and primates; dispersal behavior; conservation of endangered birds

updates.name: Jeffrey S. Fehmi
updates.bio: Professor in the University of Arizona School of Natural Resources and the Environment and program chair for Ecology, Management and Restoration of Rangelands. His research follows rangelands from degraded to self-sustaining states, covering restoration and reclamation methods, how disturbance drives degradation, and detecting rangeland change. PhD in wildland resource science, UC Berkeley.
updates.research_interests: rangeland restoration and reclamation methods; links between disturbance and degradation; detecting rangeland change; invasive species and disease ecology; restoration and fire ecology

updates.name: Jennifer L. Tank
updates.bio: Galla Professor of Biological Sciences at the University of Notre Dame and, since 2016, director of the Notre Dame Environmental Change Initiative. Her lab examines how human activity alters stream and river ecosystem function, including nutrient and carbon cycling, agricultural conservation practices such as cover crops and two-stage ditches, and experiments at ND-LEEF. AAAS Fellow (2020).
